surprises.description: Pentair reported adjusted EPS of $1.18, well above the preview’s $1.07 consensus and the $1.05–$1.08 guidance range. The beat was substantially larger than the preview’s in-line-to-slightly-soft base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.18 significantly exceeded the company's guidance range of $1.05 to $1.08.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Consensus: $1.07”; the preview also says the “print itself is nearly pre-ordained” and its base case is “in line with guide.”

surprises.description: Pool sales fell 18%, a much smaller decline than the preview’s expected 25% decline and $266 million estimate. Management said the completed destock, rather than weak demand, was the primary driver; the roughly $280 million destock was larger than the preview’s approximately $250 million estimate, but it was completed by the end of Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pool sales declined 18% year-over-year to $291 million … driven primarily by the now-completed channel inventory destock rather than weak demand”; the destock “totaled roughly $280 million across Q2 and Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Pool consensus was “$266M” and “−25.0%”; the preview highlighted whether destocking was “actually over” and said the expected FY impact was “~$250M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income was stronger than the preview’s implied expectation: the July guidance called for a 14–16% decline, while the reported $242 million compares with $263 million a year earlier, a decline of about 8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The consensus table reports adjusted operating income “Down 14–16%”; Q3 FY2025 adjusted operating income was “$263M.”

surprises.description: Tariff refunds were much smaller than the preview’s illustrative expectation for a refund-supported quarter, and management expects none in Q4. That leaves a roughly $43 million headwind to repeat in 2027, making the EPS beat less dependent on refunds but creating a larger future comparison headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 results benefited from only $8 million in tariff refunds versus $35 million in Q2, and management expects no further refunds in Q4, creating a ~$43 million headwind to repeat in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “a $1.07 ‘in-line’ print built on $20M+ of refunds is a lower-quality beat”; it also cited a FY expectation of “$35–$50M.”

surprises.description: Water Solutions delivered strong profit and margin growth despite only $6 million of tariff refunds: segment income rose 16% and ROS expanded 370 basis points to 29%. This was better than the preview’s concern that unusually high prior-quarter margins might not prove durable once refunds faded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water Solutions sales grew 1% to $422 million with segment income up 16% to $121 million and ROS expanding 370 bps to 29%, aided by $6 million in tariff refunds and 4% commercial growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Margin durability ex-Pool, and how much is tariff refunds,” noting Q2 margins were “flattered by ~$35M of IEEPA tariff refunds.”

surprises.description: Flow sales were materially below the preview’s estimate, and management attributed the shortfall to delayed food and beverage spending. However, segment income and ROS still improved, so the miss was concentrated in revenue rather than profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flow sales rose 4% to $262 million with segment income up 15% and ROS expanding 250 bps to 26%, though results came in slightly below expectations due to delayed food and beverage spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Flow sales of “$274M” and “+8.9%.”

surprises.description: The 2027 Pool outlook was slightly below the preview’s roughly 16% growth framing: management projected about 14% growth. But it said that growth could be achieved with flat sell-through and no market recovery, offering support for the forecast despite the preview’s concern that a flat market could undermine it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Pool to deliver approximately $180 million of year-over-year sales growth (about 14%) in 2027 even assuming flat sell-through of ~$1.45 billion and no market recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$1.45B of 2027 Pool revenue” versus ~$1.25B in 2026, “roughly +16%,” and highlighted whether that framework would survive a flat pool market.

surprises.description: Taco financing left pro forma net leverage slightly higher than the preview’s expected level, and the stated deleveraging target was less aggressive: about 2.5x leverage and a 1.5–2x goal, rather than approximately 2.4x at close and a sub-1.5x target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Taco was financed with $1.4 billion in term loan debt at ~5.25% interest, raising pro forma net leverage to ~2.5x with a plan to delever to 1.5-2x over the next 24 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~2.4x at Taco close” and “a sub-1.5x target within two years.”
